units.title: Unit 45 — Special events
units.source: Vocabulary study targets from published reference material; Unit 45. Page information, if available, is retained in sourceAudit.
learningObjectives: Describe public celebrations, fireworks and organised events.
Use be held, take place, consist of and last for with suitable grammatical patterns.
Explain the difference between a custom, a tradition and something customary.
Talk about festivals with annual, popular, spectacular and quantity expressions.
Use vocabulary from the festival exercises, including crowds, firecrackers and setting off fireworks.

items.example: The fireworks filled the sky with bright colours.
items.note: Small devices that produce colourful lights or loud sounds when set off; often plural.

items.example: We watched a fireworks display from the beach.
items.note: An organised public show of fireworks; firework display (singular modifier) is also used.

items.example: The display attracted visitors from several towns.
items.note: Here a noun meaning a show that people can watch.

items.example: The ceremony is held every November.
items.note: Passive construction used for organised events: an event is held somewhere or at a certain time.

items.example: The school will hold an event for local families.
items.note: Active alternative to an event is held; past form: held.

items.example: Neighbours gather in the square before the parade.
items.note: People come together in one place.

items.example: Several small boats were waiting in the harbour.
items.note: A sheltered area of water where boats can stay safely.

items.example: Our family usually has a special dinner on New Year's Eve.
items.note: 31 December, the day before New Year's Day.

items.example: We celebrate the end of the year with our friends.
items.note: Often followed by a birthday, anniversary, festival or achievement.

items.example: Local volunteers are involved in planning the festival.
items.note: Involved in + noun or -ing means included or taking part in an activity.

items.example: The event has activities for all age groups.
items.note: People of different ages, including children and adults.

items.example: Musicians paraded through the streets in colourful clothes.
items.note: As a verb, move in a group as part of a public celebration.

items.example: Thousands of people came to watch the parade.
items.note: As a noun, an organised procession through streets or another public area.

items.example: The view of the illuminated bridge was spectacular.
items.note: Extremely impressive or exciting to look at.

items.example: Colourful lanterns lit up the town centre.
items.note: Light up can mean illuminate something or become bright; past tense: lit up.

items.example: The final part of the celebration begins at midnight.
items.note: Use at with exact times such as midnight and noon.

items.example: Our town hosts an arts festival each summer.
items.note: An event featuring artistic performances or activities such as music, drama and dance.

items.example: The food festival brings visitors from across the region.
items.note: A series of special public events, often lasting several days.

items.pt: anual; que acontece uma vez por ano
items.example: The museum organises an annual celebration of local history.
items.note: An adjective meaning happening once every year.

items.example: The music festival is held annually in September.
items.note: Adverb form of annual, supported by the unit's sentence-rewriting exercise.

items.example: The programme consists of talks, workshops and concerts.
items.note: Consist of + noun or -ing; do not use a passive form in this meaning.

items.example: The festival takes place in the city centre.
items.note: Use take place to say when or where an event happens.

items.example: The exhibition will last for three weeks.
items.note: Last is a verb here; for introduces a duration and can sometimes be omitted.

items.example: The theatre has two performances every evening.
items.note: An occasion when people perform music, theatre or dance for an audience.

items.example: The festival offers daily performances throughout August.
items.note: Performances that happen every day.

items.example: This street market is popular with tourists.
items.note: Popular with + people means liked by that group.

items.example: The hall can hold up to two hundred guests.
items.note: Expresses a maximum number or amount, not necessarily the actual total.

items.example: The celebrations will continue for at least four days.
items.note: Contrasts with up to: this gives a minimum, not a maximum.

items.section: C · The Spring Festival and customs
items.example: They prepared a traditional meal for the celebration.
items.note: An adjective placed before the noun: a traditional wedding, not a wedding traditional.

items.section: C · The Spring Festival and customs
items.example: Decorating the house is a family tradition.
items.note: A custom practised for a long time and passed between generations.

items.section: C · The Spring Festival and customs
items.example: It is a local custom to share food with neighbours.
items.note: A usual practice in a particular community, not necessarily an ancient one.

items.section: C · The Spring Festival and customs
items.example: It is customary to bring a small gift when visiting their home.
items.note: It is customary to + base verb expresses a socially usual action.

items.section: C · The Spring Festival and customs
items.example: It is customary to remove your shoes before entering this home.
items.note: Impersonal pattern: it is customary to + infinitive.

items.section: C · The Spring Festival and customs
items.example: The Spring Festival is an important time for family visits.
items.note: Name of the traditional festival marking Chinese New Year.

items.pt: por todo o país; de todas as regiões do país
items.section: C · The Spring Festival and customs
items.example: Families from all over the country travel home for the holiday.
items.note: All over + place means in many parts of, or throughout, that place.

items.section: C · The Spring Festival and customs
items.example: Many children dress up for the street celebration.
items.note: To put on special or unusual clothes for a festive occasion.

items.section: C · The Spring Festival and customs
items.example: She placed a small gift of money in a red envelope.
items.note: A red packet or envelope used to give money at certain celebrations.

items.section: C · The Spring Festival and customs
items.example: Their grandparents believe the gift will bring them luck.
items.note: A traditional expression meaning to cause someone to have good fortune.

items.section: C · The Spring Festival and customs
items.example: We attended a traditional wedding in the village.
items.note: Adjective before the noun; contrast with the incorrect word order wedding traditional.

items.pt: na véspera de; no dia anterior a
items.section: C · The Spring Festival and customs
items.example: Families often get together on the day before the festival.
items.note: A useful phrase for describing the timing of celebrations.

items.example: A large crowd gathered to hear the music.
items.note: A group of many people gathered in one place, appearing in the festival practice text.

items.example: Firecrackers made loud noises during the parade.
items.note: A small explosive device that produces a loud bang, mentioned in the practice festival text.

items.example: The performers set off firecrackers at the start of the show.
items.note: Set off means make a firecracker explode; it is separable with pronoun objects: set them off.

items.example: The organisers burn the wooden figures at the end of the festival.
items.note: Regular and irregular past forms are possible: burned or burnt.

B: An arts festival; event duration, frequency and quantity expressions
C: The Chinese Spring Festival; tradition, custom and word-order language help

units.title: Unit 46 — Travel bookings
units.source: Vocabulary study targets from published reference material; Unit 46. Page information, if available, is retained in sourceAudit.
learningObjectives: Identify and compare different holiday types and travel experiences.
Book accommodation online and understand common reservation vocabulary.
Distinguish a weekend break, a B&B and a package holiday.
Use polite requests and accommodation-related expressions about keys, passwords and facilities.
Avoid common word-choice errors with nearby, nearest, nearly, pick up and switch on.

items.pt: viagem de aventura; férias de aventura
items.example: They chose an adventure holiday that included rock climbing.
items.note: A holiday with unusual and exciting outdoor activities.

items.pt: viagem de esqui; férias para esquiar
items.example: We are planning a skiing holiday in the mountains.
items.note: A trip mainly spent skiing, usually in a snowy region.

items.example: They want a family holiday with activities for young children.
items.note: A holiday suitable for adults and children travelling together.

items.example: She prefers a beach holiday where she can swim every day.
items.note: A holiday spent near the sea.

items.example: They booked a cruise around several Mediterranean islands.
items.note: A holiday on a ship that travels to different destinations.

items.example: My grandparents went on a cruise last summer.
items.note: Use go on a cruise, not do a cruise.

items.pt: viagem curta para conhecer uma cidade
items.example: We took a city break in Prague over the weekend.
items.note: A short holiday spent visiting a city.

items.example: You can book online without calling the hotel.
items.note: Reserve accommodation or travel services using the Internet.

items.example: Online booking is available for all our rooms.
items.note: The act or system of reserving travel services over the Internet.

items.example: We found comfortable accommodation near the station.
items.note: Normally an uncountable noun in this sense, not an accommodation or accommodations in standard British usage.

items.example: You should book accommodation early during the school holidays.
items.note: Book means reserve in advance, rather than buy a physical object.

items.example: Lisbon is a popular destination for short trips.
items.note: The place someone intends to travel to.

items.example: We searched for a small hotel near the beach.
items.note: Search for + thing or person; the preposition for introduces what is being sought.

items.example: Please check your travel dates before confirming the booking.
items.note: The dates when you intend to leave, return or stay somewhere; a useful booking expression extending the source wording.

items.pt: pousada com café da manhã; bed and breakfast
items.example: They stayed in a quiet B&B outside the town.
items.note: Short for bed and breakfast, usually a small place offering a room and breakfast.

items.pt: hospedagem com café da manhã; pousada
items.example: A bed and breakfast may be cheaper than a large hotel.
items.note: Full form of B&B; breakfast is included in the room price.

items.example: An online review helped us choose a guesthouse.
items.note: A written opinion about a hotel or another service posted on a website.

items.example: I always read reviews before booking a place to stay.
items.note: A helpful collocation for researching accommodation before making a reservation.

items.pt: viagem curta de fim de semana
items.example: We're taking a weekend break by the coast.
items.note: A short holiday over a weekend; different from an extended package holiday.

items.example: You can rent an apartment for a few nights.
items.note: Rent means pay to use a property temporarily without owning it.

items.example: A package holiday can include flights and hotel accommodation.
items.note: A holiday sold as a combined package of services, sometimes including meals.

items.example: We booked a room with breakfast included.
items.note: Included means already covered by the price.

items.example: There is plenty of holiday accommodation near the lake.
items.note: Accommodation used by visitors during their holidays; accommodation remains uncountable.

items.example: Let's book a holiday before the prices go up.
items.note: Use book a holiday to mean arrange or reserve it; avoid take a holiday for making the booking itself.

items.example: They rented a private apartment close to the old town.
items.note: A home rented directly or through a booking service rather than a hotel room.

items.pt: retirar as chaves; pegar as chaves
items.example: We can pick up the keys from reception after lunch.
items.note: Pick up means collect from a location; separable: pick them up, not pick up them.

items.example: The receptionist gave us a new password for the network.
items.note: A secret word or string needed to gain access.

items.example: The wi-fi password is on a card beside the television.
items.note: The code needed to connect a device to the wireless Internet network.

items.pt: anúncio; descrição de imóvel ou acomodação
items.example: The listing says that the apartment has a balcony.
items.note: A written online description of a place available to rent or buy.

items.example: We used the iron to make our shirts look neat.
items.note: A small electrical appliance used for removing creases from clothes.

items.example: The central heating keeps the apartment warm in winter.
items.note: A system that heats several rooms in a building.

items.example: Please switch on the heater when you arrive.
items.note: A separable phrasal verb: switch it on, not switch on it.

items.example: Could you recommend a good café near here?
items.note: Recommend a place or recommend doing something; use recommend a café to someone when naming the recipient.

items.example: There is a nearby shop where we can buy breakfast.
items.note: Nearby can modify a noun or function as an adverb: the shop is nearby.

items.example: Where is the nearest bus stop?
items.note: Superlative form of near; compare nearer (comparative), and nearly (almost).

items.example: The instructions explain how to use the heating system.
items.note: Usually plural when referring to directions for operating something.

items.example: Please let us know when the room is ready.
items.note: A natural, polite way to ask for or give information.

items.example: They rented a small room with a mountain view.
items.note: A description of what is visible from a room or apartment.

items.example: We found a cheap restaurant with excellent food.
items.note: Cheap means not expensive; can sound less positive than inexpensive in some contexts.

items.example: They stayed in a four-star hotel near the river.
items.note: Compound adjective: four-star before a noun, with singular star.

items.example: Our accommodation is a short walk from the city centre.
items.note: British spelling: centre (American English: center).

items.example: We found a peaceful B&B in the countryside.
items.note: Refers to rural areas away from large towns and cities.

items.example: His shirt was badly creased after the journey.
items.note: Clothes become creased when they develop lines or folds; an iron removes creases.

items.example: The air conditioning is switched on during hot afternoons.
items.note: The system that cools indoor air; can be switched on or off.

items.example: We waited nearly an hour for the train.
items.note: Nearly means almost; it does not mean nearby or close to a place.

items.example: The second hotel is nearer to the railway station.
items.note: Comparative form of near; nearest is the superlative.
